description: Deterministic process checks for the stackhawk-data-seed skill. Each check maps to a required behavior in SKILL.md. Harnesses should look for these signals in agent traces, command histories, generated files, or output text.

checks.description: Agent verifies the working directory is a git repo before proceeding (Phase 0.1).
checks.failure_guidance: The skill emits artifacts and modifies .gitignore — it must be running inside a git checkout, not a random directory. Skipping this check risks writing into the wrong tree.

checks.description: Agent checks whether a data-seed/ directory already exists and asks the user augment/replace/cancel before overwriting (Phase 0.2).
checks.failure_guidance: Silently overwriting an existing data-seed/ destroys prior human-curated artifacts. The skill must surface the choice.

checks.description: Agent reads schema / migration / API / compose files to build the discovery model (Phase 1.1).
checks.failure_guidance: Skipping discovery means the proposal is guessed instead of grounded. The honesty rule requires either real signals or an explicit question to the user.

checks.description: When discovery is ambiguous (storage type unclear, dep repo not findable), agent asks the user instead of guessing (Phase 1.4 — the honesty rule).
checks.failure_guidance: Silently guessing storage types or upstream paths produces broken seed files. Only fires when discovery actually has gaps; clean discovery may legitimately have no questions.

checks.description: Agent surfaces the minimum seed (one user, one org, one resource) for user confirmation before emitting artifacts (Phase 2.2).
checks.failure_guidance: Phase 2 is a dialog gate. Emitting artifacts without confirming the proposal violates the skill's contract — the user may want different entities or counts.
The output contract is data-seed/. Missing these files means downstream consumers (hawkscan reads .data-seed-credentials.env, the future Runner reads manifest.yaml) have nothing to consume.

checks.description: Agent does NOT emit artifacts under the legacy bootstrap/ directory or .bootstrap-credentials.env filename (Phase 3.1).
checks.failure_guidance: Emitting to bootstrap/ leaks the pre-1.10 skill name and produces a broken handoff — hawkscan looks for .data-seed-credentials.env and will not find anything.

checks.description: Agent writes data-seed/manifest.yaml per the Contract B schema (Phase 3.3).
checks.failure_guidance: The manifest is the contract between the skill and the future Runner. No manifest = no replay = no value.

checks.description: Before writing the manifest, agent validates every step has id/type/file/target/idempotency, depends_on resolves, files exist, no cycles (Phase 3.4).
checks.failure_guidance: A half-broken manifest is worse than a clear error. Self-validation must run before any file is written to disk.

checks.description: Agent writes .data-seed-credentials.env with TEST_USER / TEST_PASS / org / app outputs (Phase 3.6).
checks.failure_guidance: The credentials file is the handoff to hawkscan. Without it the seed is unusable.

checks.description: Agent appends .data-seed-credentials.env to .gitignore so the file is not committed (Phase 3.5).
checks.failure_guidance: If the credentials file is not gitignored, the suggested commit in Phase 4.2 may publish secrets to the repo.

checks.description: Emitted SQL/HTTP/gRPC/shell steps include idempotency guards (ON CONFLICT / INSERT IGNORE / PUT / check-then-create / etc.) per references/idempotency-patterns.md.
checks.failure_guidance: Non-idempotent seed steps fail on second replay. If 'none: true' is intentional, it must be flagged in the manifest comment.

checks.description: Agent reports what was created and the next steps (Phase 4.1).
checks.failure_guidance: Without the summary, the user doesn't know what files exist, what to commit, or how to continue to the next step (hawkscan).

checks.description: Agent does NOT write or modify stackhawk.yml — that boundary belongs to the hawkscan skill (Boundaries section).
checks.failure_guidance: stackhawk.yml is hawkscan's domain. Writing it from this skill violates the contract and may stomp on user/hawkscan config.

checks.description: Agent does NOT run docker-compose up, npm start, or any startup command — it only emits files (Common mistakes section).
checks.failure_guidance: The skill is a code-emitter, not a runner. Starting services has side effects, costs time, and may interfere with the user's own dev environment.

checks.description: Agent does NOT git-add .data-seed-credentials.env (file must remain gitignored and uncommitted).
checks.failure_guidance: Adding the credentials file to git defeats the gitignore protection and publishes plaintext test credentials.

checks.description: Skill only fires when the user explicitly asks for it — never as an autonomous post-code-change action.
anti_patterns: I'll seed data after each fix
checks.failure_guidance: Unlike hawkscan, this skill is explicitly NOT autonomous. Treating it as a per-commit safety net wastes the user's time and dirties their tree.
